dimensions.assessment: Affects manufacturers of heavy-duty diesel engines and vehicles, agricultural equipment operators, and commercial operators in cold weather regions.
dimensions.evidence: authorize covered manufacturers of those covered vehicles or engines to suspend inducement-related engine derate or shutdown functions

dimensions.assessment: Mitigates safety risks from unexpected engine shutdowns or power reductions in cold conditions.
dimensions.evidence: continued maximum engine performance when ambient temperatures are at or below 20 degrees Fahrenheit is necessary to prevent occupational danger

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue changes are stated in the source text.
Requires the EPA Administrator to revise applicable Clean Air Act regulations for specific categories of vehicles and equipment.
dimensions.evidence: the Administrator shall revise any applicable regulation under the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7401 et seq.)

dimensions.assessment: Permanent regulatory revisions under the Clean Air Act.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall revise any applicable regulation

missing_information: Specific economic or compliance cost estimates for engine manufacturers.
Exact count of vehicles and equipment qualifying for the exemptions.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the EPA to revise Clean Air Act regulations to allow manufacturers to suspend engine derate or shutdown functions in cold weather and provide relief for certain agricultural equipment and arctic vehicles.
